column3: Trick number three is the strangest. Rig the test, and then believe the result.
At Stanford, students held their arm in ice cold water for as long as they could. Then they spent a minute on an exercise bike.
Then came a fake lesson. After exercise, the change in how long you can take the cold reveals your heart type. And one type means a healthier, longer life.
One group heard healthy hearts last longer. The other heard healthy hearts give up sooner.
Then they went back in the water.
Most of them shifted, in exactly the direction that meant a healthy heart.
Think about that. Holding on longer on purpose can't change your heart. It only changes the score.
So were they doing it on purpose? On an anonymous survey, only nine of thirty eight admitted trying.
And most of the people who denied it walked away believing they had the healthy heart.
That's the trick. You do something to get the answer you want, and somehow, it doesn't feel like you did anything at all.
